subject: AsterLabs dedicated-node eviction pattern — remediation, credits & follow-up plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Turner <emma@asterlabs.com>, ops@asterlabs.com
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: AsterLabs dedicated-node eviction pattern — remediation, credits & follow-up plan

Hi Emma / AsterLabs SRE team,

Thanks again for working with us while your dedicated pool experienced degraded throughput earlier today. I wanted to summarize what we observed, the immediate mitigations we applied, and the follow-up commitments from Redwood. I will coordinate a live RCA and runbook walk-through if that is helpful.

What happened (summary)
- Window: 2026-09-01T13:02:00Z to 2026-09-01T14:08:00Z.
- Symptom: burst of 503s and elevated p95 latency for generation requests to your reserved GPU pool.
- Immediate cause: an autoscaler configuration change introduced last week increased node termination aggressiveness for idle GPUs; combined with a traffic spike of long-sequence inference requests this caused rapid KV cache churn and cache evictions, resulting in significantly longer warmup for new allocations and a queued backlog.
- Knock-on: our scheduler retried in rapid succession, increasing pressure on the pool and causing temporary fallback to a hosted model variant for a subset of your traffic.

Actions taken during incident
- Rolled back the autoscaler change at 13:18Z to stop pending evictions.
- Temporarily throttled parallel long-sequence jobs coming from your routing policy to reduce cache thrash.
- Initiated a controlled drain and warm restart of 3 hot nodes showing cache fragmentation.
- Routed noncritical traffic to a compatible hosted variant to preserve SLA for external customers.

Customer impact
- AsterLabs saw increased p95 latency and intermittent 503s for approximately 66 minutes. Some internal AsterLabs customers reported timeouts in batch processing jobs.

Short-term remediation and offer
- We are preparing a targeted credit: two days of prorated reserved capacity applied to your next invoice. If you prefer a different structure, tell us and we will work it out.
- Attached: incident-timeline-asterlabs-20260901.pdf and eviction-logs-asterlabs-20260901.tar.gz for your post-analysis.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute RCA call on 2026-09-03 at 10:00 AM PT.

Planned permanent mitigations
- Autoscaler: tighten the idle termination window and add an eviction-smoothing buffer to avoid correlated evictions across a tenant pool.
- Warmup: implement selective proactive KV prefill for long-sequence customers during predicted busy slots.
- Routing: add a short-circuit fallback to a warmed standby variant for critical flows to avoid user-visible 503s.
- Canary: deploy the autoscaler change to a single canary tenant before broad rollout; Redwood will invite AsterLabs to the canary cohort if you prefer.

Next steps from my side
- Share raw incident timeline and SRE runbook (attached).
- Schedule the RCA call for 2026-09-03 10:00 AM PT unless you prefer another time.
- Begin work now on the autoscaler smoothing change and provide daily progress updates until the canary is live.

Thanks, and sorry for the disruption — we take this seriously.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident-timeline-asterlabs-20260901.pdf (PDF, 180KB)]
[Attachment: eviction-logs-asterlabs-20260901.tar.gz (logs, 22MB)]

From: Emma Turner <emma@asterlabs.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Crouse <john.crouse@asterlabs.com>, ops@asterlabs.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AsterLabs dedicated-node eviction pattern — remediation, credits & follow-up plan

Vivek,

Thanks for the quick write-up and the attachments. We appreciate the rollback and the temporary routing you put in place. A couple of asks from our side before the RCA call:

1) Can you quantify the exact traffic split that was rerouted to the hosted variant and the p50/p95 delta experienced by those requests? Our downstream customers saw retry storms and we need the numbers to reconcile.
2) The two days of credit is a start but given material customer impact we will likely ask for a larger goodwill gesture as part of the postmortem. Please have someone from billing ready on the call.
3) We are particularly concerned about recurrence during our Black Friday equivalent (we have a heavy batch window mid-November). What concrete changes will prevent this class of incident under high concurrency?

We can do the RCA call 2026-09-03 10:00 AM PT. Putting this on my calendar.

- Emma
Director of Engineering, AsterLabs
emma@asterlabs.com
[On-call: john.crouse@asterlabs.com]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Turner <emma@asterlabs.com>, John Crouse <john.crouse@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, ops@asterlabs.com
Date: 2026-09-02T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AsterLabs dedicated-node eviction pattern — remediation, credits & follow-up plan

Emma, John,

Quick answers ahead of the call:

1) Reroute quantification
- Approximately 18% of requests matching your high-concurrency generation route were rerouted to the hosted variant between 13:20Z and 14:05Z. The hosted variant saw median latency increase of ~45ms and p95 increase of ~220ms relative to baseline; importantly we saw near-zero error rate for the hosted traffic once routing took effect. We will share the request-level CSV in the RCA packet.

2) Credits and billing
- We will have billing on the RCA call. As an immediate gesture, we are proposing two full days of prorated reserved capacity as a starting point; if you quantify additional business impact we will discuss an adjusted package.

3) Concrete recurrence mitigations (short list)
- Autoscaler smoothing: add a distributed delay to node termination decisions across a tenant's nodes so we never evict many nodes from a single pool within a small window.
- Proactive KV warming: for identified long-sequence tenants, prefill KV on standby nodes during expected traffic surges.
- Routing rewrite: add a fast-path fallback to warmed standby variants for user-facing endpoints.
- Canary cadence: implement small-tenant canaries for autoscaler changes with a 72-hour monitoring window and automatic rollback on p95 regressions.

I will bring the request-level telemetry and the logs. Camila and Ben will walk through the planned autoscaler smoothing patch and the rollout timeline on the call.

Attachments: remediation-checklist.md (brief)

Regards,
Vivek

[Attachment: remediation-checklist.md (text, 6KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: internal: AsterLabs follow-ups and canary priority

Team,

Filing notes from the customer thread and setting priorities before the RCA call. Action items:
- Camila: lead autoscaler smoothing patch. Target branch by 2026-09-06, canary deploy by 2026-09-08.
- Marissa: own the KV prefill prototype. Need a minimal safe rollout plan by 2026-09-10.
- Neha: run the traffic replay to validate routing fallback for long sequences, share results by EOD 2026-09-04.
- Vivek: coordinate billing contact and confirm credit wording with finance on the call.

Also set up a daily 30-minute sync until the canary is healthy; please indicate your availability. I will also prep a short customer-facing timeline we can publish after the RCA.

Ben
VP, Customer Engineering

From: Emma Turner <emma@asterlabs.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Crouse <john.crouse@asterlabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AsterLabs dedicated-node eviction pattern — remediation, credits & follow-up plan

Vivek, Ben, Camila,

Thanks for the detail and the timeline. We accept the two days of prorated reserved capacity as an initial credit and will discuss additional remediation compensation on the RCA call.

We are OK for the 10:00 AM PT call — please send a calendar invite and include the billing representative and the on-call SREs. For the canary, we would like to be invited so we can validate behaviour against our November batch window in a staging shadow run.

AsterLabs will bring incident logs showing downstream customer retries; John will lead that portion. Looking forward to the RCA.

Best,
Emma Turner
Director of Engineering, AsterLabs
emma@asterlabs.com
